mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate over three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy stance, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (t-test p > 0.10) during periods when FEDFUNDS rises for three consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters indicates weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and results in negative S&P 500 returns over the subsequent 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 falls for two consecutive quarters
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 declines for two consecutive quarters (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A rapid increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) above 6% within a single month signals deteriorating labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profitability, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above 6% in one month
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% in a single month (t-test p > 0.10).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below its 12-month moving average for four consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness, which depresses earnings and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 12-month moving average for four consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during periods of sustained industrial production contraction (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL above their respective 12-month averages signals a dual tightening of monetary policy and rising inflation, which increases real discount rates and reduces equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL both exceed 12-month averages
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when both FEDFUNDS and CPIAUCSL exceed their 12-month averages (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated rise in both personal income (implied by PAYEMS) and retail sales (implied by RSAFS) above their 12-month moving averages over two consecutive months signals strengthening consumer demand, which boosts corporate earnings and results in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS and RSAFS both exceed 12-month moving averages for two consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly positive when both PAYEMS and RSAFS exceed their 12-month moving averages for two months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent decline in the household survey unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 5% for three consecutive months signals a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and inflation expectations, leading to higher discount rates and negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE remains below 5% for three consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Housing Starts index (HOUST) above its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months signals a recovery in residential construction activity, which boosts related equities and leads to positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: HOUST > 12-month moving average for five consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when HOUST exceeds its 12-month moving average for five consecutive months (t-test p > 0.05).
